clippings.speaker: John Carpenter
clippings.quote: Debra introduced me to Dean, who is a tremendously talented cameraman. Kind of a strange guy to deal with, and can be sarcastic on the set, but wow, what a cameraman.
clippings.title: On John Carpenter + Career Retrospective Interview
clippings.context: Word-association career interview by Justin Beahm for Fangoria's John Carpenter Legends issue, reposted in full on Beahm's site in 2016.

clippings.speaker: John Carpenter
clippings.quote: He and I discovered the Panavision anamorphic fast lenses together on ESCAPE FROM NEW YORK. It was a moment of pure joy when we discovered we could open the lenses to 2.2 or 1.8, and could shoot a scene in the middle of Ventura Boulevard. at midnight. You couldn’t do that before. … It changed how we made film.
clippings.title: On John Carpenter + Career Retrospective Interview
clippings.context: Same Fangoria Legends interview, continuing his answer to the prompt 'Dean Cundey'.

clippings.speaker: John Carpenter
clippings.quote: [Dean Cundey] doesn't know. He has no idea. He puts the lights up. He puts the lights up and we were in the snow. He has no clue. … You tell him that. Tell him he's full of shit.
clippings.title: John Carpenter Says ‘The Thing’ Cinematographer Is ‘Full of S—‘ Over His Ending Theory: He ‘Has No Clue,’ Only I Do and ‘I Cannot Tell You’
clippings.context: Carpenter teasingly dismissing Cundey's 'eye gleam' theory of The Thing's ending; originally said to ComicBook.com and reported by Variety.

clippings.speaker: Dean Cundey
clippings.quote: Working with John was a revelation because suddenly here was a guy who was interested in using the camera in a creative way, drawing the audience in. … I thought, Boy, this is just my cup of tea, where the camera is contributing and you’re telling the story with visuals.
clippings.title: The Making of John Carpenter's Halloween
clippings.context: David Konow's oral history of Halloween built from interviews from years past; first published October 2016, republished 2018.

clippings.speaker: Dean Cundey
clippings.quote: in the case of John, he was not afraid of having dark areas in the frame because he understood the importance. Compared to other directors, who would say, “Well, it’s dark, I can’t see the wall in the corner back there”, and so it was a case of being allowed the flexibility to experiment.
clippings.title: The Den Of Geek interview: Dean Cundey
clippings.context: Cundey on shooting in the dark on Halloween and The Thing, in a career interview with Simon Brew.

clippings.speaker: Dean Cundey
clippings.quote: When I first started with him on Halloween, I had worked on a lot of low budget movies, but he was the first director (I worked with) who I think really realized what visual storytelling was, how to use the camera to engage the audience and to tell the story. So I really appreciated that immediately. And you know, I think that continued, because we did five movies where that followed through.
clippings.title: [Interview] Cinematographer Dean Cundey on the Art of Illusion in Film
clippings.context: Interview by Matt Artz at the H40: Forty Years of Terror Halloween 40th anniversary convention.

notes: Carpenter's side is thin online; the 1998 American Cinematographer 'common language' quote appears only on a wiki and was not used.
